newsitem.title: USA: U.S. money managers boost cash positions -- MCM.
newsitem.headline: U.S. money managers boost cash positions -- MCM.

text.p: U.S. fixed-income managers modestly increased their dollar-weighted durations on their debt portfolios, and cash positions reversed recent downward trends in the latest week, an MCM MoneyWatch Inc survey said.
In the week ending July 7, cash as a percentage of assets rose to 3.07 percent from 2.75 percent registered the previous week.
"This puts (cash positions) back to the levels of May," said MCM MoneyWatch vice president Astrid Adolfson, who conducts the weekly survey.
"There appears to have been some profit taking and governments are now seen as more underweighted," Adolfson added.
In addition, durations as a percentage of benchmark crept up to 108.1 from 108.0 percent.
A duration reading above 100 percent indicates the group of investors polled is mostly long on the market.
A portfolio's duration represents its average maturity and is used by portfolio managers to calculate exposure to risk.
In the "next likely move" category, portfolio managers representing 31 percent of total assets in the survey said they would "buy," slightly lower from 32 pecent in the prior week.
Strategists leaning toward "sell" held steady at 19 percent.
Fifty percent of managers said they were "neutral" on the market.
The survey showed 32 percent of investors polled overweighted the 10-plus years duration sector, down from 33 percent the previous week, while 10.0 percent underweighted it.
The remaining 58 percent were "neutral."
In the five- to 10-year duration sector, 49 percent of investors polled said they overweighted the securities and 10 percent underweighted them.
The survey included 38 domestic participants who manage about $110 billion in fixed-income assets. The poll is conducted weekly by MCM and usually is released on Tuesday.
